sections.title: 一、詞彙（佔15分）
sections.instructions: 說明︰第1至15題，每題選出最適當的一個選項，標示在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。每題答對得1分，答錯不倒扣。

groups.passage: The pineapple, long a symbol of Hawaii, was not a native plant. [[21]], pineapples did not appear there until 1813. Natives planted the fruit across South and Central America and in the Caribbean region, [[23]] Christopher Columbus first found it. Columbus brought it, along with many other new things, back to Europe with him. From there, the tasty fruit [[24]] throughout other parts of civilization. groups.passage:
The Paralympics are Olympic-style games for athletes with a disability. They were organized for the first time in Rome in 1960. In Toronto in 1976, the idea of putting together different disability groups [[26]] sports competitions was born. Today, the Paralympics are sports events for athletes from six different disability groups. They emphasize the participants’ athletic achievements [[27]] their physical disability. The games have grown in size gradually. The number of athletes [[28]] in the Summer Paralympic Games has increased from 400 athletes from 23 countries in 1960 to 3,806 athletes from 136 countries in 2004.
The Paralympic Games have always been held in the same year as the Olympic Games. Since the Seoul 1988 Paralympic Games and the Albertville 1992 Winter Paralympic Games, they have also [[29]] in the same city as the Olympics. On June 19, 2001, an agreement was signed between the International Olympic Committee and the International Paralympics Committee to keep this [[30]] in the future. From the 2012 bid onwards, the city chosen to host the Olympic Games will also host the Paralympics.

tags.topic: the history and growth of the Paralympic Games

sections.title: 三、文意選填（佔10分）
sections.instructions: 說明：第31至40題，每題一個空格，請依文意在文章後所提供的 (A) 到 (J) 選項中分別選出最適當者，並將其英文字母代號標示在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。每題答對得1分，答錯不倒扣。

groups.passage:
Familiar fables can be narrated differently or extended in interesting and humorous ways. The end of the famous fable of “The Tortoise and the Hare” is well known to all: the tortoise wins the race against the hare. The moral lesson is that slow and steady wins the race. We all have grown up with this popular version, but the [[31]] fable can be extended with different twists. At the request of the hare, a second race is [[32]] and this time, the hare runs without taking a rest and wins. The moral lesson is that [[33]] and consistent will always beat slow and steady. Then it is the tortoise that [[34]] the hare to a third race along a different route in which there is a river just before the final destination. This time, the tortoise wins the race because the hare cannot swim. The moral lesson is “First [[35]] your strengths, and then change the playing field to suit them.”
But the story continues. Both [[36]] know their own drawbacks and limitations very well; therefore, they jointly decide to have one last race—not to decide who the winner or loser is, but just for their own pleasure and satisfaction. The two [[37]] as a team. Firstly, the hare carries the tortoise on its back to the river. Then, the tortoise carries the hare and swims to the [[38]] bank of the river. Lastly, the hare carries the tortoise again on its back. Thus they reach the [[39]] line together. Overall, many moral lessons from the last match are highlighted. The most obvious one is the importance of [[40]]. Another moral which also means a great deal is “competition against situations rather than against rivals.”

tags.topic: an extended version of the fable “The Tortoise and the Hare” and its moral lessons

sections.title: 四、閱讀測驗（佔32分）
sections.instructions: 說明︰第41至56題，每題請分別根據各篇文章之文意選出最適當的一個選項，標示在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。每題答對得2分，答錯不倒扣。

groups.passage:
To Whom It May Concern:
Your address was forwarded to us by Why Bother Magazine. All of us here think The International Institute of Not Doing Much is the best organization in the world. You know how to avoid unnecessary activities!
We closely followed the advice in your article. First, we replaced all our telephones with carrier pigeons. Simply removing the jingle of telephones and replacing them with the pleasant sounds of birds has had a remarkable effect on everyone. Besides, birds are cheaper than telephone service. After all, we are a business. We have to think of the bottom line. As a side benefit, the birds also fertilize the lawn outside the new employee sauna.
Next, we sold the computers off to Stab, Grab, Grit, and Nasty, a firm of lawyers nearby. Our electricity bill went way down. Big savings! The boss is impressed. We have completely embraced paper technology. Now that we all use pencils, doodling is on the increase, and the quality of pencilwomanship is impressive, as you can tell from my handwriting in this letter. By the way, if you can, please send this letter back to us. We can erase and reuse it. Just tie it to <u>Maggie</u>’s leg and she’ll know where to take it.
Now it’s very calm and quiet here. You can notice the difference. No more loud chatter on the telephones! All we hear is the scratching of pencil on paper, the sound of pigeons, and the delivery of inter-office correspondence by paper airplane.
Wonderful! I’ve always wanted to work for an insurance company ever since I was a little girl. Now it’s perfect.
Sincerely yours,
Eleanor Lightly
Spokeswoman and Company Hair Stylist
ABC Activity Insurance: Insure against overdoing it

groups.passage:
The Galápagos Islands are the Pacific island paradise where Darwin’s theory of evolution was born. They are places filled with giant tree lizards, sandy beaches, and tropical plants. Now they will be famous for one more thing: the world’s first green airport.
This group of islands off the coast of Ecuador has recently contracted Argentine Corporación America to manage the redevelopment of the airport on the island of Baltra. It is estimated that US$20 million is needed to complete <u>the project</u> by 2009. The new development has several important features: use of wind and solar energy, passive heating and cooling systems, as well as concrete runways in place of asphalt, which has a greater carbon footprint during its production cycle. This new development couldn’t be coming at a better time for the Galápagos, which were added to an environmental “danger list” in 2007.
Pacific islands like the Galápagos, Easter Island, and Tahiti, have economies that are driven almost completely by tourism. However, some people think these are “unsustainable models of development.” The number of visitors to the Galápagos rose more than 250% from 1990 to 2006, while the number of commercial flights to the area rose 193% from 2001 to 2006. These increases put great stress on the islands’ resources and environment. Air travel is especially criticized for exhausting natural resources and causing environmental damage. Thus, efforts are being made to reduce the environmental impact of the tourism industry. The greening of airports is just one of these attempts.

options.B: The background of building a green airport.
options.C: The history of the Galápagos Islands.
options.D: The ease of transportation to the Pacific islands.

options.D: They have become one of the most dangerous places in the world.

groups.passage:
According to popular folklore, many animals are smarter than they appear. Dogs bark before earthquakes; cattle predict rainfall by sitting on the ground. But cattle may have another hidden talent in telling which way is north.
Small animals such as mole rats living underground are known for the use of magnetism to navigate. Dr. Begall and her colleagues wanted to know whether larger mammals also have the ability to perceive magnetic fields. They investigated this possibility by studying images of thousands of cattle captured on Google Earth, a website that stitches together satellite photographs to produce an image of the Earth’s surface.
Grazing animals are known to orient themselves in a way that minimizes wind chill from the north and maximizes the warmth of the sun when they are cold. The researchers therefore had to study a lot of cows grazing in lots of different places at different times of day, in order to average out these factors and see whether cattle could act like compass needles.
The researchers concluded that cattle do generally orient themselves in a north-south direction. This north-south preference has also been noted in flies, termites and honeybees. But unfortunately, even the high resolution of Google Earth is not powerful enough to tell which end of the cow is its head, and which its tail. The researchers were therefore unable to answer their research questions of whether cattle prefer to look north or south, and whether that differs in the northern and southern hemispheres.

questions.stem: What is the article mainly about?

options.B: Whether cattle are superior to other animals.
options.D: Whether cattle behave like compass needles.

questions.stem: Which of the following factors might affect Dr. Begall’s research result?

options.D: Google Earth is a reliable research tool.

questions.stem: Why couldn’t the researchers get the answer to their research questions?

options.A: Many cattle in their study were sitting on the ground.
options.B: The cattle constantly change directions to avoid wind chill.
options.C: There is magnetic difference between the two hemispheres.
options.D: They couldn’t tell a cow’s head from its tail in the satellite pictures.

tags.topic: cattle aligning their bodies north-south, studied with Google Earth images

groups.passage:
Children normally have a distrust of new foods. But it’s the parents’ job to serve a variety of foods and expose their children to healthy dieting habits.
Some simple strategies can help even the pickiest eater learn to like a more varied diet. First of all, you don’t have to send children out of the kitchen. With hot stoves, boiling water and sharp knives at hand, it is understandable that parents don’t want children in the kitchen when they’re making dinner. But studies suggest that involving children in meal preparation is an important first step in getting them to try new foods. In one study, nearly 600 children from kindergarten to sixth grade took part in a nutrition curriculum intended to get them to eat more vegetables and whole grains. The researchers found that children who had cooked their own foods were more likely to eat those foods in the cafeteria than children who had not. Kids don’t usually like radishes, but if kids cut them up and put them in the salad, they will love the dish.
Another strategy is not to diet in front of your children. Kids are tuned into their parents’ eating preferences and are far more likely to try foods if they see their mother or father eating them. Given this powerful effect, parents who are trying to lose weight should be careful of how their dieting habits can influence a child’s perceptions about food and healthful eating. In one study of 5-year-old girls about dieting, one child noted that dieting involved drinking chocolate milkshakes, because her mother was using Slim-Fast drinks. Another child said dieting meant “you fix food but you don’t eat it.” By exposing young children to <u>erratic</u> dieting habits, parents may be putting them at risk for eating disorders.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of this article?

options.A: To explain what causes children’s eating disorder.
options.B: To teach children about the meal preparation process.
options.C: To advocate the importance of vegetables and whole grains.
options.D: To inform parents how they can help their children like varied foods.

questions.stem: Which of the following groups will eat more balanced meals?

options.A: The children who help cook food.
options.B: The children whose parents are on a diet.
options.C: The children who do not love radishes.
options.D: The children whose parents work in a cafeteria.

questions.stem: What does <u>erratic</u> in the last sentence imply?
Which of the following is true about Slim-Fast?

options.B: It looks like a chocolate milkshake.
options.C: It contains a variety of vegetables.
options.D: It is intended for slim, fast people.

tags.topic: strategies to help picky children accept a varied, healthy diet

sections.title: 一、翻譯題（佔8分）
sections.instructions:
說明：1.請將以下兩題中文譯成正確而通順達意的英文，並將答案寫在「答案卷」上。
2.請依序作答，並標明題號，每題僅能譯成一個英文句子。每題4分，共8分。

stats.source: stats-3.xls 第一題(滿分:8分)，翻譯題兩小題合計

questions.label: 翻譯1
questions.stem: 大部分學生不習慣自己解決問題，他們總是期待老師提供標準答案。
questions.answer: Most students are not {used to / in the habit of} solving problems by themselves {; / and} they always expect their teachers to provide (them with) standard answers.
questions.scoring_notes:
本題型測驗目標為評量考生將中文句子譯成正確、通順、達意英文的能力。第一句評量的重點在於考生是否能運用熟悉的字詞（例如：解決問題、期待、提供、標準答案等）寫出以Most students為主詞的基本句型
評分標準：
1. 本大題總分 8 分，每小題滿分 4 分。
2. 各部份獨立且各為 1 分；每個錯誤扣 0.5 分，各部份扣完為止。
3. 相同之拼字錯誤只扣一次。
4. 句首未大寫或標點符號不妥，各扣 0.5 分，只扣一次。
5. 若未依提示將中文句子譯成一個英文句子，扣 0.5 分。
註1：{ }（大括弧）表示皆為可使用之字詞。

patterns: be not used to / be not in the habit of + V-ing
tags.topic: students relying on teachers for standard answers instead of solving problems themselves

sections.title: 二、英文作文（佔20分）
sections.instructions:
說明︰1.依提示在「答案卷」上寫一篇英文作文。
2.文長120個單詞(words)左右。

figures.label: 提示右方的圖片
figures.description: 黑白照片（無任何文字）：一棟房屋倒塌成廢墟。屋頂整個塌陷，木造屋樑與椽條斷裂、歪斜交錯地垂落；由石塊、土塊砌成的牆崩落，碎石、磚塊與斷裂的木條堆滿前景地面。畫面左側殘存一段抹成白色的外牆，牆面有一道明顯的長裂縫，牆上有一扇窗戶；中間殘存的石牆上有一個拱形門洞，透過門洞可見屋內也已坍塌。左下角一名頭戴斗笠（臉被斗笠遮住）、身穿長袖上衣與深色長褲的人，背著一個編織的大簍子（背簍），從瓦礫堆旁走過。背景是光禿的樹枝與灰白的天空。題本未說明事件原因，畫面看起來像地震等天災過後倒塌的民宅。

questions.label: 英文作文
questions.stem:
提示︰
請根據右方圖片的場景，描述整個事件發生的前因後果。文章請分兩段，第一段說明之前發生了什麼事情，並根據圖片內容描述現在的狀況；第二段請合理說明接下來可能會發生什麼事，或者未來該做些什麼。
questions.scoring_notes:
評分標準：
本大題總分 20 分，主要在評量考生描述圖片的能力，重點在於評量考生掌握時式用法（tenses）的語法能力及使用適當詞彙、句型以「描述事件」、「談論問題並提出解決之道」，寫出一篇具連慣性、統一性的英文作文。採整體式評分，分為五等級：特優（19-20 分）、優（15-18 分）、可（10-14 分）、差（5-9 分）、劣（0-4 分），閱卷委員於閱讀完考生試卷後，於腦海裡產生一個整體（holistic）分數，再以分項式評分標準檢閱是否符合整體印象分數，分項式評分指標包含下列 5 項：內容（5 分）、組織（5 分）、文法、句構（4 分）、字彙、拼字（4 分），及體例（2 分）（詳見表 1）。另外，字數不足，扣 1 分；未依提示分段，扣 1 分。
表 1：英文作文分項式評分指標
項目＼等級｜優｜可｜差｜劣
內容｜優：主題(句)清楚切題，並有具體、完整的相關細節支持。(5-4 分)｜可：主題不夠清楚或突顯，部分相關敘述發展不全。(3 分)｜差：主題不明，大部分相關敘述發展不全或與主題無關。(2-1 分)｜劣：文不對題或沒寫(凡文不對題或沒寫者，其他各項均以零分計算)。(0 分)
組織｜優：重點分明，有開頭、發展、結尾，前後連貫，轉承語使用得當。(5-4 分)｜可：重點安排不妥，前後發展比例與轉承語使用欠妥。(3 分)｜差：重點不明、前後不連貫。(2-1 分)｜劣：全文毫無組織或未按提示寫作。(0 分)
文法、句構｜優：全文幾無文法錯誤，文句結構富變化。(4 分)｜可：文法錯誤少，且未影響文意之表達。(3 分)｜差：文法錯誤多，且明顯影響文意之表達。(2-1 分)｜劣：全文文法錯誤嚴重，導致文意不明。(0 分)
字彙、拼字｜優：用字精確、得宜，且幾無拼字錯誤。(4 分)｜可：字詞單調、重複，用字偶有不當，少許拼字錯誤，但不影響文意之表達。(3 分)｜差：用字、拼字錯誤多，明顯影響文意之表達。(2-1 分)｜劣：只寫出或抄襲與題意有關的零碎字詞。(0 分)
體例｜優、可（合併一格）：格式、標點、大小寫幾無錯誤。(2 分)｜差：格式、標點、大小寫等有錯誤，但不影響文意之表達。(1 分)｜劣：違背基本的寫作體例或格式，標點、大小寫等錯誤甚多。(0 分)
註2：改編自張武昌等（民 93）「英文寫作能力測驗規劃研究（VI）」研究報告。台北：大考中心。95 年學測在「項目」部分修訂。

tags.topic: a house in ruins after a disaster (likely an earthquake): what happened before, the present situation, and what may happen or should be done next

extraction.method: 題本：python-docx 讀 paper-2.doc（soffice 轉 docx）為主，與 pdftotext -layout paper-1.pdf 逐段比對，並用 Read 看題本 PDF 第 1–8 頁影像確認空格位置、底線與版面；作文圖片以 pdfimages 抽出後放大檢視並轉寫文字描述；底線字以 docx run 格式（w:u）與頁面影像交叉確認；答案：pdftotext answer.pdf；評分原則：pdftotext scoring.pdf + Read 看第 2–4 頁影像（翻譯參考答案為大括弧排列、作文評分表為圖片，人工轉寫；表 1 另以 pdfimages 抽出原圖放大核對）；統計：xlrd 讀 stats-1（P/Ph/Pl/D）、stats-2（選項分析 T 列）、stats-3（非選擇題分數分布），並程式核對選項分析的星號選項與官方答案一致、答案選項選答率等於答對率 P、分數分布人數加總等於到考人數
issues: 結構與 gsat-spec.json legacy_gsat 94–110 期別一致：詞彙 1–15（各1分）、綜合測驗 16–30（3篇×5題，各1分）、文意選填 31–40（A–J，各1分）、閱讀測驗 41–56（4篇×4題，各2分）、翻譯題 2題×4分、英文作文 20分；選擇題 72 分＋非選擇題 28 分＝100 分。題本封面：考試時間 100 分鐘、選擇題共 56 題、非選擇題共 2 大題、選擇題答錯不倒扣。
翻譯題與作文的題號：題本第貳部分翻譯題印「1.」「2.」，作文沒有題號；為避免與選擇題 1、2 重複（validator 要求 no 為整數、label 不可重複），no 依序編為 57、58、59（非題本題號），label 用「翻譯1」「翻譯2」「作文」，與 gsat-97 等相鄰年份一致。

翻譯參考答案在 scoring.pdf 第 2 頁是大括弧排列的圖片，已人工轉成一行文字：{ } 內以「 / 」分隔可互換的字詞（依原註 1「{ }（大括弧）表示皆為可使用之字詞」）；( ) 照原圖保留——本年度註腳只定義大括弧，「(them with)」的括號依慣例應為可省略之字詞，但官方未明文說明。翻譯1 的「{; / and}」表示兩個子句之間用分號或 and 連接；翻譯2 最後一組選項中的「skills/abilities」斜線為原圖文字（非轉寫分隔符號）。

翻譯參考答案原圖以虛線把每題切成四個計分部分（對應評分標準 2「各部份獨立且各為 1 分」），轉成一行時虛線無法保留，特此記錄切分位置——翻譯1：① Most students are not {used to / in the habit of} ｜② solving problems by themselves {; / and} ｜③ they always expect their teachers ｜④ to provide (them with) standard answers.；翻譯2：① {In addition to / Besides} studying hard ｜② to {gain / obtain / get} knowledge, ｜③ students should also develop ｜④ {independent thinking skills/abilities. / the ability to think independently.}
翻譯題 scoring_notes：scoring.pdf 原文為同一段說明兩句（「第一句評量的重點在於…；而第二句在測驗…」），兩小題各取與本題相關的部分，其餘（評分標準 1–5 與註 1）兩題相同。scoring.pdf 重抄的翻譯題說明與題本一致。

作文 scoring_notes：評分說明照 scoring.pdf 第 3 頁逐字，原文「具連慣性、統一性」的「連慣性」（應為「連貫性」）照原文保留；表 1 為圖片表格（第 4 頁），逐列轉寫為「項目｜優：…｜可：…｜差：…｜劣：…」，表頭寫成「項目＼等級｜優｜可｜差｜劣」；「體例」列的優、可兩欄在原表合併為一格。註2 為原文腳注（本年度文字為「95 年學測在「項目」部分修訂」）。本年度作文評分另載明「字數不足，扣 1 分；未依提示分段，扣 1 分」（無 97 年的書信格式扣分）。
作文圖片（題本第 7 頁、scoring.pdf 第 3 頁同一張黑白照片）已轉為 figures 文字描述；題本與評分說明都沒有交代事件原因，描述中「看起來像地震等天災過後倒塌的民宅」為依畫面所作的判斷，作文 tags.topic 同此。
作文提示中「之前」「現在」「接下來」「未來」在題本為粗體加底線、翻譯說明中「每題僅能譯成一個英文句子」為粗體加底線，屬強調格式，依 schema 不保留。提示文字在題本是方框內分行排版，stem 依 Word 原檔合併為「提示︰」＋一段文字。
畫底線的字：第 44 題 Maggie（選文中粗體加底線，選文為斜體手寫字型）、第 48 題 the project、第 55 題 erratic 在選文與題幹皆為粗體加底線（docx run 格式與頁面影像確認），題目即針對這些字詞發問，故選文與題幹都以 <u>…</u> 標出；斜體、粗體本身不保留。

非選擇題統計（stats-3.xls）只有大題層級的分數人數分布（第一題＝翻譯題兩小題合計，滿分 8；第二題＝作文，滿分 20），放在 s5、s6 的 score_distribution（schema 未定義的延伸欄位，percent 已換成 0–1 小數，分母為報名總人數 141858，含缺考 2346）；小題 stats 為 null。原表級距字串如「9.00- 9.99」的多餘空白已去除；作文「20.00-20.00」列在原表為空白，依累積人數（19.00-19.99 累積 24 人＝該列人數）判定為 0 人，填 count 0、percent 0。兩題各級距人數加總皆等於到考人數 139512。

選擇題 stats：correct_rate＝P、high_group＝Ph（前33%）、low_group＝Pl（後33%）、discrimination＝D（stats-1.xls 英文工作表）；option_rates 取 stats-2.xls 英文工作表選項分析的 T（全體）列，原表為整數百分比，加總因四捨五入不一定等於 1，未答比例（第 45、56 題為 1%，其餘 0%）未收錄。已程式核對 56 題選項分析標星號的選項與 answer.pdf 一致，且該選項比例等於 P。
題本各題組前的「41-44 為題組」等標示未放入 passage（題組範圍可由 questions 題號得知）。第 41–44 題選文為信件，信末「Sincerely yours,」、署名、職稱、公司名與標語各自一行，照題本分行保留。
第 15 題選項題本印作「(A ) blessing」（括號內多一個空白），選項代號照常記為 A。

照題本原文保留、非抽取錯誤：第 45–48 題選文「Argentine Corporación America」（America 無重音符號）、第 26–30 題選文「International Paralympics Committee」（正式名稱為 International Paralympic Committee）、第 41–44 題選文「pencilwomanship」（作者刻意造字）。
paper-2.doc（docx）與 pdftotext paper-1.pdf 的題幹、選項、選文逐段比對一致；兩者對翻譯題說明「2.」前、作文說明「2.」前的分行不同（docx 為同一段），依 PDF 題本版面以換行分隔，與相鄰年份處理方式相同。
